title: Cap. IV Arg. 9 Sol: owed conclusion is foresight-election; Major imperfect if made universal
pass_a_gloss: Solution. It is to be observed that in no argument of the Remonstrants does the owed conclusion come forth. For it is one thing to conclude, Therefore the decree concerning believers to be saved is the very election itself to salvation; another, Therefore the very election itself to salvation is made from foresight of antecedent faith. This conclusion we have waited for in vain, which has nowhere been seen to appear. But let us discuss the aforesaid reason, such as it is. The Major explains the reason of Election quite imperfectly; nor is it true throughout, if it be understood universally, as it ought, unless we wish a slippery syllogism to be thrust upon us. Let it therefore be made universal, in this way: Every decree of God concerning human salvation whose foundation is Christ is the very election itself of singular persons to salvation. Let the Minor be attached, But the decree concerning believers to be saved (that is, any men whatsoever, if they believe) is that decree of salvation whose foundation is Christ: Therefore this decree concerning Believers to be saved is the very election itself of singular persons to salvation.
pass_b_english: Sol. Notice: in no Remonstrant argument does the owed conclusion appear. One thing is to conclude that the decree to save believers is election itself; another, that election itself is from foresight of antecedent faith — the conclusion we waited for in vain and never saw. Discuss their reason as it stands. The Major explains election quite imperfectly, and is not true throughout if taken universally as it must be, unless we let a slippery syllogism be forced on us. Make it universal: every divine decree on human salvation whose foundation is Christ is election itself of singular persons to salvation. Attach the Minor: the decree to save believers (any men, if they believe) is that Christ-founded salvation decree. Therefore that decree is election itself of singular persons.
source_text: Sol. Observandum est, in nullo argumento Remonstrantium debitam conclusionem prodire. Nam aliud est concludere, Ergo decretum de salvandis credentibus est ipsissima electio ad salutem; aliud, Ergo Electio ipsissima ad salutem fit ex praevisione fidei antecedaneae. Hanc conclusionem frustra exspectavimus, quae nusquam visa est comparere. Sed rationem praedictam, qualem qualem, discutiamus. Major imperfecte admodum explicat rationem Electionis; nec vera est usquequaque, si universaliter intelligatur, sicuti oportet, nisi syllogismum vaders velimus nobis obtrudere. Fiat ergo universalis, hoc modo, Omne Dei de salute humana decretum cujus fundamentum est Christus, est ipsissima singularium personarum electio ad salutem. Attexatur Minor, At decretum de salvandis credentibus (id est, quibuslibet hominibus, si credant) est illud decretum salutis cujus fundamentum est Christus: Ergo hoc decretum de salvandis Credentibus est ipsissima singularium personarum electio ad salutem.
